nodes.summary: If `d` is the path-length dissimilarity of `T` on its leaves and `d` is symmetric, `bmeLength T d = length T`. Symmetry is needed because `bmeLength` averages the two orientations of each pair.
nodes.title: The balanced minimum-evolution length of a tree metric is the tree length

nodes.summary: Pauplin's formula (Pauplin 2000): the total edge length of a binary tree with real edge lengths is `∑_{i<j} 2^{1-τ_ij} d_T(i, j)`, the sum over pairs of leaves of the path length weighted by `2` to the power one minus the number of edges on the path.
nodes.title: Pauplin's formula

nodes.summary: The balanced minimum-evolution length of the topology of `T` for a dissimilarity `d` (Desper and Gascuel 2002): `∑_{i<j} 2^{1-τ_ij} (d(i, j) + d(j, i)) / 2`. It depends on `T` only through the topological distances `τ_ij`. Each term is symmetrized, so the value does not depend on the orientation `T.pairs` happens to assign to a pair: swapping the children of a node, or the two sides of the root edge, leaves…
nodes.title: Balanced minimum-evolution length

nodes.summary: Kraft equality for unrooted binary trees: for every leaf `i` of a tree with distinct leaf labels, `∑_{j ≠ i} 2^{1-τ_ij} = 1`.
nodes.title: Kraft equality

nodes.summary: Kraft's equality for a rooted binary tree: `∑_{leaves} 2^{-depth} = 1`.
